Privacy Policy

Effective date: November 21, 2026

Last updated: November 21, 2026

OpenMarkdown is run by Xueyan Zhang, an individual in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada ("we", "us"). We decide how the data described here is used, so we are responsible for it. To ask anything about privacy, email support@openmarkdown.dev.

The short version

  • The app collects nothing. No account, no analytics, no telemetry. Your notes are plain files on your computer.
  • Anywhere is opt-in. If you create an account, only the one folder you pick goes to our servers.
  • Encrypted, not end-to-end. Synced notes are encrypted in transit and at rest. Only your signed-in account and the AI apps you authorize can read them. Our servers can read them too, because they have to in order to merge edits and answer your AI app. That is why we don't call it end-to-end.
  • We don't look at your notes, except when you ask us to for support, when the law requires it, or to investigate a specific security incident or abuse report (section 3).
  • No selling, no ads, no AI training on your notes.
  • Marketing email only if you tick the box. Signing up does not subscribe you.

The rest of this page gives the details.

1. The app (no account)

The app has no AI inside it and sends no analytics or telemetry. It makes two kinds of network request:

  • Update check. When it starts, the app asks GitHub, where our releases are published, whether there is a new version. Like any web request, this shows GitHub your IP address. No account or identifier is sent.
  • Feedback you send. Only when you write a message and press Send. We get exactly what is on screen: your message, a short context line (app version, operating system, channel, and your plan if you are signed in) that you can edit or delete first, and your email if you add one.

Everything else, including your files, what you type and how you use the app, stays on your computer. Our Transparency page lists everything the app touches on your machine.

2. Anywhere and Anywhere+ (with an account)

WhatWhyWhere it lives

Waitlist entry: your email address, if you join the Anywhere beta waitlist on our websiteTo invite you when a beta spot opensWorkOS (sign-in provider)

We don't collect anything else. In particular we don't track what you do inside the app, and we don't read the parts of your computer you didn't choose to sync.

3. Encryption, and who can read your notes

  • Data travels over encrypted connections (TLS) and is encrypted when stored. The keys are managed by Cloudflare, our hosting provider.
  • This is not end-to-end encryption. Our servers can read your synced notes. They have to: merging edits from two devices, and answering an AI app's request to search or change a note, both need the text.
  • Who can read your notes: you, when you are signed in; the AI apps you have connected; and our servers, automatically, to do the jobs above.
  • When a person (the founder) might look at your notes:
    1. You ask for help and give permission to look at specific notes. We look only at what is needed and only for as long as needed.
    2. The law requires it, for example a valid court order. Unless the law forbids it, we will tell you first.
    3. To investigate a specific security incident or a specific report of serious abuse, such as illegal content or an attack carried out through our service. We look only at what is needed for that investigation, and we tell you afterwards unless the law forbids it.
  • What we see without opening notes: for billing and support we can look up an account's plan record and how much space it uses. This does not show the contents of notes.

4. AI apps you connect

When you connect Claude (Anthropic) or ChatGPT (OpenAI) to Anywhere, the AI app gets access to your synced folder. It can list, search, read, add to and change notes there, and read your plan and usage. It cannot buy, upgrade or cancel anything for you.

  • Whatever the AI app reads from your notes goes to that company and is handled under its privacy policy and your settings with it, not ours. Check those settings, for example whether your chats are used for model training.
  • We don't send your notes to any AI company on our own. Notes reach an AI app only when you have connected it and it asks for them.
  • We don't use your notes to train any AI model, and we don't let our service providers do so.
  • You can disconnect an AI app at any time in its settings.

5. Service providers we use

We use a small number of companies to run OpenMarkdown. They process data for us, under contract, only to provide their service.

Some of these providers are in the United States or other countries outside Canada, so your data may be stored or processed there and be subject to those countries' laws. Where the law requires it (for example GDPR), we rely on the providers' standard data-transfer safeguards.

We don't use a separate email-sending service for account notices or newsletters yet. If we add one, we will list it here before we use it.

We don't sell personal information or share it with anyone for their own advertising.

6. Email we send

  • Service email. Receipts, payment problems, security notices, plan-expiry reminders and notices about changes to these policies. These are part of running your account, not marketing. You get them while you have an account.
  • Marketing email (opt-in only). Our newsletter: new versions, new blog posts and occasional offers, about once a month. After you first sign in, a welcome step asks whether you want it, with a box that is not ticked. Agreeing to our Terms does not sign you up. If you never tick the box, you won't get marketing email from us.
  • You can withdraw at any time with the unsubscribe link in every marketing email or by emailing us.

8. Your rights

Depending on where you live (for example under Canada's PIPEDA, the EU and UK GDPR, or California law), you can:

  • ask what personal data we hold about you and get a copy;
  • correct it;
  • delete it, subject to the records we must keep;
  • take your data with you. Your notes are already plain Markdown files on your computer;
  • object to or limit some uses, and withdraw consent (such as for marketing) at any time.

Email support@openmarkdown.dev. We will answer within 30 days. We may need to confirm it is really you first.

If you aren't happy with our answer, you can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or to the data protection authority where you live.

Legal bases (EU/UK). We handle account and sync data to provide the service you signed up for (contract). We keep logs and handle security for the service's legitimate interests. We keep billing records to meet legal obligations. We send marketing email only with your consent.

9. Security

We protect data with encrypted connections, encrypted storage, signed-in access to each account's own data only, and checks on every payment notification. No system is perfectly secure. If a breach puts your personal information at real risk, we will tell you and the relevant authorities as the law requires.

10. Children

OpenMarkdown accounts are not for anyone under 16. You can use the app without an account at any age. If we learn that a child has created an account, we will delete it.

11. Our website

openmarkdown.dev counts page visits with a privacy-friendly tool that uses no cookies and collects no personal data, only total views, referrer and country. The home page shows a Product Hunt badge, which loads an image from Product Hunt, so their server sees your IP address. The feedback form sends only what you write, and your email if you add it, when you press Send. Payment links open Stripe's pages, which have their own privacy policy. The "Join the beta waitlist" button on the Anywhere page opens the sign-up page of our sign-in provider, WorkOS, which keeps your waitlist entry (section 2).

12. Changes to this policy

If we make a change that matters, we will tell you by email or in the app before it takes effect. Previous versions are available on request: email support@openmarkdown.dev. We won't start using data you already gave us in a significantly different way without asking you first.
